deities: Shirgul Maharaj (incarnation of Shiva, worshipped as Chureshwar Mahadev)

history.summary: Historic hill shrine atop Churdhar Peak (3,647 m / 11,965 ft), the highest peak of the outer Himalayas, on the Sirmaur-Shimla border. Devotion to Shirgul Maharaj as an incarnation of Shiva is centuries old; locals believe the temple existed in some form since the early medieval period, though the present structures have been renovated repeatedly (verify). Sources disagree on whether a formal idol or lingam was ever established here - one recent account says some claim no idol exists at all - so antiquity details are unverified (verify). CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Sirmaur'; the shrine is in Himachal Pradesh.

name: Shirgul Maharaj Temple
town_description: Churdhar is the 3,647-metre summit of the highest peak in the outer Himalayas, reached only by trekking via Nohradhar, Chopal or Haripurdhar. The trail passes through villages, fields and alpine meadows with panoramic views toward Badrinath, Kedarnath and the Gangetic plains.
tradition: Shaivite folk tradition (Shirgul as Shiva incarnation)

travel.airport: Jubbarhatti (Shimla) or Chandigarh airports, then road to Nohradhar/Chopal
travel.railway: Solan or Kalka railway stations, then road
travel.road: Road to trailheads at Nohradhar (Sirmaur), Chopal/Chaupal or Haripurdhar; 7-18 km trek to the summit depending on route

visitor_information.best_time: May to October, when the trek is accessible
visitor_information.opening_hours: One listing reports 4:00 AM-8:00 PM daily (verify on site)
